summary: Plan written to plan.md. MarketFront is four 7-high tiers facing west and stepping up the bluff. Each tier's deck is a railed terrace for the one above: decks at y 6, 13, 20, 28, the top one a plaza flush with Pike Place, with planters and a bronze pig. Above sit white housing with timber fins and the older white-brick market building. Plot 1 is the Overlook landing: zigzag 9-wide stairs between terraces at y 2, 9, 16, 23, landscaped banks, and a concrete-and-glass lift tower. Each tier's west face repeats glass, timber and grey stone, the concept's look of glowing stacked shopfronts at dusk. MarketFront is four west-facing tiers (grey stone base, spruce-and-glass bands) stepping up the bluff to a flush Pike Place plaza with the bronze pig, planters and benches. Above the tiers stand white housing with balconies, the quartz-brick old market and the lift towers. The hillclimb plot is zigzag stair terraces with planted banks and a HILLCLIMB glass tower, lit at dusk by froglight glow, lanterns and candles.

Shell and massing: parts/shell0.mjs builds the plot 0 masonry in site coordinates: W0 stepped retaining walls, tiers T1/T2/T3/T3N with a lit air strip behind each west face, the plaza deck at y28, H housing, M1 and M2.
make.sh gives 101,857 placed, no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. `mcd check` reports 0 floating blocks. I only looked at the front-elevation render tile.
polish: H north/south/east windows are not carved (only the west door and window cells are air).
M1 floors at y40 and y46 are full smooth_stone, so quartzWindow sills at those y will be refused; P4 should skip them or use replace.
Ring quartz_bricks sits at y52 on M1; cornice stairs and parapet at y53+ are left to P4.
H roof interior at y42 is bare (smooth_stone deck at y41, parapet at y42 only on the edge); the green roof and iron_bars belong to P4.
Tier canopy cells (x20, 41, 69, 76/83 at F+6..F+7) are untouched.
Only the front elevation render was viewed; the other tiles were not inspected.
No stair cuts in the T2/T3 decks for SH, TW or K; those parts must carve or build around them.

summary:
Hillclimb landing: Plot 1 (Hillclimb landing) built in parts/plot1.mjs: terraces D0 to D3 (terraceMass, footprint-clipped), zigzag stairs S10, S21 and S32 (9 wide, 7 treads each, landings flush), and the N planted slope (three grass and moss steps with polished_andesite faces, a few oaks).
Also two bench rows, five lamp posts on deck tops, and the D3 east edge opened for the bridge. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; Hillclimb landing reports 0 refused and 0 off-palette; no fit issues inside plot 1; zoomed renders read as terraces with stairs.
Stair zones are cleared of rail posts and seats after the terraces are built, and the flights go in first, so the fit check no longer reports "stairs end short".
polish: Planted banks along the terrace south and west faces (3 deep, inside the lower terrace) are not built: the terrace decks are smooth_stone and plantedBank needs air and does not clip to the footprint.
Lawn and paving on the D0 landing plaza: D0 is smooth_stone, not the lawn and paving the plan lists.
Lamp posts every 9 along the terrace rails are not built; only the five stair-head lamps are, and the stair-head lamp at x44 z44 is skipped (it sits off the deck).
The stair-head cheeks are polished_andesite from stairFlight, so the deck cells under the stair zones read as polished_andesite, not smooth_stone (visible only at the stair edges).
plot 0 has 105 'on a bottom slab' fit issues near x96 z154+ (grass_block over bottom slabs); they are not in plot 1 and belong to the shell or plaza part.

waste.cost: about 10 coordinate checks by eye; one wrong guess first put the stairs on the wrong edges
waste.tool: a plot-local helper in vocab (box(x0,x1,z0,z1) and inside/ground callbacks that take plot coordinates) so parts never add PLOT1[2] by hand

summary:

The HILLCLIMB (ET) and PIKE PLACE MARKET (M1) plaques are NOT placed: both boards fall on cells owned by earlier parts or the plaque helper places nothing in air.
Checks: `mcd check` reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks. `mcd fit` printed nothing matching my filter. I viewed only the left elevation, where the dusk strips are not visible until the glass exists.
polish: ET HILLCLIMB plaque not placed: its board plane (wall x 63, y 29..35, z 189..197) is P3's glass, so it needs P3 to leave that band air or a board in front of it. The plaque helper also needs at least 7 rows for block letters.

M1 market sign not placed: plaque on the west face at x 178/179 (y 44..54, z 4..23) placed 0 cells in every position tried, even with width 20 / height 2 or 7. Its board needs a solid wall behind it on P1's shell, and runParts refuses writes into P1 cells.

No room-level light check: rooms.json has no rooms, so `mcd light`/`mcd room` were not run. The lantern and candle spacing is by eye.
plan.md checklist left unticked for P6 because the signs are missing; elements.md item 20 is marked done, items 18 and 21 are not ticked.

summary:
inspection: Fixed the 105 FIT "on a bottom slab" issues: retainingWall's cap was a bottom polished_andesite slab with its planter grass one block above, leaving half a block of air. Added an opt-in `cap: "block"` (default unchanged) in vocab/h2.mjs and passed it from the three W0 calls in parts/shell0.mjs.
Rebuilt with ./make.sh: FIT now reports "fit: OK", and WALK reports ok: true with rooms [] (start 59, reachedCells 6024).
Also, make.sh logged plaza notes (planter beds clipped or skipped off-deck) and dusk sign skips; these are not in the listed problems and were left alone.

waste.what: The fit check printed only about 6 of the 105 issues, so I had to work out the cause from the cell coordinates (x=96 is plot-local x 15) and by reading retainingWall in vocab/h2.mjs to see that its cap is a bottom slab with a planter one block up.
waste.cost: About 4 tool calls of reading and grepping; no blocks placed by hand.
waste.tool: fit should group the issues by the helper or part that placed the block (e.g. 'retainingWall cap in shell0.mjs:47, 49 x 105') and print a --all flag for the full list.

waste.what: Checking which callers of retainingWall would be affected by a change meant grepping parts/ and vocab/ by hand.
waste.tool: A fit line naming the helper call site (file:line of the retainingWall call) would have located the fix directly.
